Larry Rhoden

Republican candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, South Dakota · Incumbent

Governor of South Dakota (incumbent); rancher

Larry Rhoden is the Republican governor of South Dakota. He was lieutenant governor from 2019 and became governor in January 2025 when Kristi Noem resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security. He won the Republican nomination by beating Toby Doeden in a July 28, 2026 runoff and is running with Lt. Gov. Tony Venhuizen against Democrat Dan Ahlers.

Where Rhoden stands

Property taxes
Says the 2026 property tax bills he backed are the largest property tax cut in state history. Says Senate Bills 245 and 96 together cut homeowners' property taxes by 34% on average statewide.
Carbon pipeline / eminent domain
Signed a law that bans carbon-capture pipeline projects from using eminent domain to get access to private land.
Prison construction
Proposed a $650 million prison construction plan, asked the Legislature to approve it, and lists finishing the project as one of his accomplishments.
Affordability
Says property taxes are one of the biggest affordability concerns he hears about from residents.

Background

  • Governor of South Dakota, January 2025–present
  • Lieutenant Governor of South Dakota, 2019–2025
  • Former state legislator and school board member
  • Served six years in the National Guard
  • Rancher from Union Center, S.D.
  • Won the 2026 Republican gubernatorial runoff against Toby Doeden, about 71% to 29%
